Thought: I will manually calculate the moles of AgNO₃ used in the titration by multiplying the volume of the AgNO₃ solution by its concentration and converting the volume from cm³ to dm³, because concentration is in mol/dm³.

1. Convert the volume of AgNO₃ solution from cm³ to dm³: 
   \( 8.20 \, \text{cm}^3 = 8.20 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{dm}^3 \).

2. Calculate the moles of AgNO₃: 
   Moles = Volume (dm³) × Concentration (mol/dm³) = \( 8.20 \times 10^{-3} \times 0.1 \).

Let's perform the calculation:

\[ \text{Moles of AgNO}_3 = 8.20 \times 10^{-3} \times 0.1 = 8.20 \times 10^{-4} \, \text{mol} \]

These moles are equal to the moles of Cl⁻ in the 25.0 cm³ portion.

3. Scale up the moles of Cl⁻ to the entire 250 cm³: 
   Since the 25.0 cm³ portion represents 1/10 of the total solution, multiply the moles of Cl⁻ by 10.

\[ \text{Total moles of Cl}^- = 8.20 \times 10^{-4} \times 10 = 8.20 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{mol} \]

4. Convert the moles of Cl⁻ to grams of NaCl:
   \( \text{Molar mass of NaCl} = 58.44 \, \text{g/mol} \).

\[ \text{Mass of NaCl} = 8.20 \times 10^{-3} \times 58.44 = 0.479208 \, \text{g} \]
